question_text:
Resolve a CrashLoopBackOff failure caused by aggressive liveness probe timing (Container Orchestration (Kubernetes)).

### Defective Code:
```yaml
# Kubernetes Pod Manifest Defect
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: payment-service-13
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: payment:v1.2
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 0 # BUG: App takes 15s to warm up; probe kills it immediately
      periodSeconds: 3
      failureThreshold: 1
```

### Reported Anomaly / Error:
CrashLoopBackOff: Container killed repeatedly during bootstrap before server starts listening in Container Orchestration (Kubernetes).

Identify the root cause of the defect and provide the corrected code snippet with rationale.
correct_answer:
# Corrected Kubernetes Pod Manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: payment-service-13
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: payment:v1.2
    startupProbe: # Use startupProbe or adequate initialDelay
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      failureThreshold: 30
      periodSeconds: 2
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      periodSeconds: 10
answer_explanation: Setting zero initial delay causes liveness probes to fail during JVM/framework startup, creating a CrashLoopBackOff. A startupProbe grants warmup time.
reference_solution:
